name: Harshnath Temple
significance: A hilltop Shaiva temple on Harshagiri about 14 km from Sikar, finished in 956 CE under the Chahamana king Vigraharaja I and endowed by the Pashupata teacher Allata from donated funds. A 973 CE inscription describes the hill as Shiva's earthly counterpart to Mount Kailasa, and the shrine drew gifts from merchants working the regional trade routes.

name: Kadu Malleshwara Temple
significance: A 17th-century Shiva temple in the Malleshwaram district of Bengaluru, built in 1669 by Venkoji, step-brother of the Maratha king Shivaji, and giving the surrounding locality its name. Shivaratri draws thousands of worshippers from across the city.

name: Ghanteswara Siva Temple
significance: A small Shaiva shrine standing inside the Kapileswara temple precinct in Bhubaneswar, built in the Kalinga manner with a three-tiered pidha vimana on a triratha plan and rising only about 2.8 metres.

name: Gupteswar Cave
significance: A limestone cave shrine about 55 km from Jeypore in Koraput district, housing a two-metre Shiva lingam that devotees believe is still growing. Worship was formally established in the mid-17th century by Maharajah Veer Vikram Dev, and Mahashivaratri now brings more than two hundred thousand pilgrims up its two hundred steps.
story: Rama is said to have found the hidden lingam while crossing the Dandakaranya forest with Sita and Lakshmana and named it Gupteshwar, the god in hiding, after which it lay forgotten until a hunter stumbled on it again.

name: Ammachiveedu Murti Temple
significance: A goddess temple at Thangassery in Kollam district founded in the 15th century by the Ammachiveedu family, with the present building completed in 1968. The deity has no image: she is worshipped as two gold-clad conches on a silver-covered peedam inside a four-foot-square sanctum, and the shrine is open to worshippers of any caste or faith.
story: Oral tradition holds that a Brahmin patriarch of Parappur married a woman born under an ill-omened star, and that the deity was moved into a conch at Sasthamcotta with the instruction to found her worship wherever a tree should split open.

name: Jagannath Temple, Alwar
significance: A Vishnu temple in Alwar whose sanctum is unusual in holding two Jagannath images at once, one fixed and one movable, alongside Sitaram and Janki. Its walls and pillars carry uncommon floral motifs, and its ritual calendar differs from the Puri tradition.

name: Hanuman Garhi Temple
deity: Hanuman (in his child form on Anjani's lap)
significance: One of Ayodhya's principal shrines, reached by seventy-six steps and laid out like a four-sided fort with round bastions at its corners and a silver-worked sanctum. It is administered by the Bairagi mahants of the Ramanandi sampradaya and the Nirvani Akhara.
story: Hanuman is said to have taken up residence in a cave on this spot to keep watch over Ramkot after Rama returned to Ayodhya from his victory over Ravana.

name: Radha Damodar Temple, Vrindavan
significance: Founded in Vrindavan in 1542 by Jiva Goswami, this is one of the central shrines of Gaudiya Vaishnavism and preserves the Giriraj Shila, a Govardhan stone kept as a relic within the temple.
story: The Giriraj Shila is said to carry Krishna's own footprints and to have been handed to Sanatana Goswami by Krishna himself, so that four turns around the temple are held to equal one circuit of Govardhan Hill.

name: Gokarnanatheshwara Temple
significance: Built at Kudroli in Mangalore in 1912 by the Billava leader Koragappa and consecrated by the social reformer Narayana Guru, who brought its Shiva lingam himself, the temple was founded so that the Billava community could worship on its own terms. A 1991 rebuilding in Chola style added a sixty-foot gopuram, and the temple hosts the city's Mangalore Dasara.

name: Aisanyesvara Siva Temple
significance: A 13th-century grey sandstone shrine on a saptaratha plan in the Old Town of Bhubaneswar, close to the western wall of the Lingaraja temple. It remains in worship, and the processional image of Lingaraja is brought here on the sixth day after Shivaratri.

name: Aluvamkudi Sree Mahadeva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Gurunathanmannu in Pathanamthitta district that lay abandoned until a hunter came upon it in the 1940s. Worship was restored and is now held on the first day of every Malayalam month, with Shivaratri as the yearly festival.
story: The shrine is held to have been established by Parashurama, and local tradition says Rama performed worship at the spot.

name: Agasteeswarar Temple, Kolapakkam
significance: A Shiva temple at Kolapakkam on the western edge of Chennai, whose complex also holds shrines to the Navagrahas, the nine planetary deities.
story: The sage Agastya is said to have worshipped Shiva here, and the presiding deity takes his name from it.

name: Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Gadhada
significance: One of the six temples raised by Swaminarayan himself, opened on 9 October 1828 in the courtyard of Dada Khachar's residence at Gadhada on land the family donated. The two-storey, three-domed shrine stands on a raised plinth with an assembly hall, pilgrim lodgings and kitchens, and in 2012 became the first temple in Gujarat to receive golden spires.

name: Guru Narasimha Temple, Saligrama
significance: A Vaishnava temple at Saligrama, 22 km from Udupi, whose two-armed lion-headed image of Narasimha is carved from saligrama stone and dated to the 8th century. The Kota Brahmins of fourteen surrounding villages take this deity, rather than any human acharya, as their sole guru.
story: The deity is said to have appeared of its own accord at the foot of a pipal tree, holding conch and discus.

name: Kaliyuga Varadaraja Perumal Temple
deity: Vishnu (worshipped as Kambamperumal, a granite pillar)
significance: A Vishnu temple at Kallankurichi near Ariyalur, roughly five centuries old, unusual in that the presiding deity is not an image but a twelve-foot granite pillar known as Kambamperumal. Its Vijayanagara-period ardha mandapam carries sculpted pillars illustrating Vaishnava narratives.
story: A cowherd named Maangan is said to have found a pregnant cow beside a sacred pillar here and, directed by Vishnu, to have raised a temple around it.

name: Kalahastiswamy Temple, Uthamapalayam
significance: A Shiva temple at Uthamapalayam in Tamil Nadu notable for its wall paintings, which date to the Madurai Nayak period.
story: The shrine is said to have been built jointly by three rulers who had been at war with one another and settled their quarrel by raising it together.

name: Kalikadevi Temple
significance: A sandstone pidha deul at Kancha Sahi in the Old Town of Bhubaneswar, enshrining a four-armed goddess worshipped locally as Kali. Its dry-masonry construction places it in the 10th or 11th century, earlier than the local attribution to the Somavamsi kings, and it remains in private hands and active worship.

name: Bhandara Ghara Shrine
significance: A 16th-century shrine within the Kapileswara temple precinct at Bhubaneswar, built with a pidha-order vimana. It holds the chalanti pratima, the movable images of Vishnu and Shiva carried out in procession at festival times.

name: Laddu Baba Temple
significance: A medieval Shiva temple at Sharanakula in Nayagarh district that blends Kalinga and Dravidian forms and is a focus of Shaiva worship in southern Odisha. Unusually for a Hindu temple, its priesthood has long been drawn from lower castes; Mahashivaratri is its main festival.

name: Dashabhuja Ganapati Temple
significance: A Ganesha temple at Erandwane on Karve Road in Pune, once held by Haripant Phadke, a sardar of the Peshwas, and later given to the Peshwas as dowry. Its image is prized for a trunk turning to the right, a form regarded as rarer and more sacred, and the shrine draws large crowds through Ganesh Chaturthi.

name: Dimapur Kalibari
significance: A Kali temple completed in 1956 in Dimapur, serving as a centre of Hindu worship in Nagaland and observing Durga Puja and Kali Puja as its principal festivals.

name: Lakshmi Narasimha Temple, Bhadravati
deity: Lakshmi Narasimha (with Venugopala and Vishnu Purushottama)
significance: A soapstone trikuta temple at Bhadravati built around 1250 under the Hoysala ruler Vira Someshwara, with three sanctums and star-shaped outer walls that Adam Hardy singles out as among the finest stellate work of the dynasty. Its reliefs range across Vaishnava, Shaiva, Shakta and Vedic subjects, and it is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India.

name: Daksheswar Mahadev Temple
significance: A Shaiva temple at Kankhal, about four km from Haridwar, raised in 1810 by Queen Dhankaur of the Landaura estate and rebuilt in 1962. The complex takes in a Das Mahavidya shrine, a Ganga temple and the Daksha Ghat on the river.
story: Hindu tradition places King Daksha's sacrifice here: slighted by his exclusion from it, Shiva's wife Sati threw herself into the fire, whereupon Shiva sent Virabhadra and Bhadrakali to behead Daksha, who was later restored to life with a goat's head.

name: Bhringesvara Siva Temple
significance: An 8th-century light grey sandstone shrine at Khatuapada on the south-eastern edge of Bhubaneswar, built as a pancharatha rekha vimana on a raised platform some 26 metres long. It stands west-facing in the Dhauli foothills beside the Daya river and is now protected by Odisha State Archaeology.

name: Dirgheshwari Temple
significance: A Shakta pitha on a rocky hill in North Guwahati, built in brick between 1714 and 1744 under the Ahom king Siva Singha with Tarun Duwarah Barphukan overseeing the work. Its sanctum lies underground inside a natural cave, and the shrine, recognised by the Archaeological Survey of India, is held locally to be second in sanctity only to Kamakhya.
story: A limb of Sati is said to have fallen here after Vishnu's discus scattered her body, and the sage Markandeya is remembered as having won Durga's blessing through penance at the spot.

name: Kunnuvarankottai Kasi Visalakshi-Viswanathar Temple
significance: A Shaiva temple near Batlagundu in Dindigul district, roughly five centuries old, modelled on the Visalakshi-Viswanathar shrine at Varanasi and distinctive for its south-facing sanctum of the goddess. It is linked to Sacchidananda Bharati I, the 25th acharya of the Sringeri Sharada Peetham, who was born nearby and whose birthday is kept here each year; consecrations were held in 2001 and 2013.
story: Local tradition holds that the image was carried here from Kasi by a devotee.

name: Dhabaleswar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple on an island in the Mahanadi about 27 km from Cuttack, raised in the 10th century under the Somavamshi king Yayati Keshari and later repaired by the rulers of Athgarh. It is reached by boat or by Odisha's first hanging footbridge, and draws crowds at Shivaratri and the Bada-osha fair.
story: The name is explained by a tale in which Shiva turned a black calf white to shield a thief who had taken refuge with him, dhabala meaning white.

name: Dishisvara Siva Temple
deity: Shiva (lingam in a circular yoni pitha)
significance: A 15th-century laterite shrine built by dry masonry in Khurda district near Bhubaneswar, standing inside a private compound. Vegetation over the superstructure and cracks in its roof have left it dilapidated despite repairs by the state archaeology department.

name: Bhadra Maruti Temple
significance: A Hanuman temple at Khuldabad, about 4 km from the Ellora caves, rebuilt in white marble in the 1960s after the earlier shrine was destroyed under Mughal rule. It is one of only three known temples where Hanuman is shown sleeping, the others being at Prayagraj and Jam Sawali, and fills with pilgrims at Hanuman Jayanti and Ram Navami.
story: Hanuman is said to have fallen into bhava-samadhi here while listening to King Bhadrasena sing in praise of Rama, and to have agreed at the king's request to stay on and bless those who came.

name: Bhoothalingaswamy Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Boothapandi in Kanyakumari district, traditionally credited to the Pandya king Pasum Pon Pandyan in the first century CE. It has a temple tank, the Theppakulam, and observes a car festival with processions of its deities.

name: Bhagabati Temple, Banapur
significance: A goddess temple at Banapur in Khordha district, counted among the Shakta pithas of Odisha and reckoned to be about seven centuries old. Banapur was the seat of the Sailodbhava dynasty, and Buddhist images found in the town also connect the place with the Vajrayana tradition.

name: Lankeswari Temple
significance: A Shakta shrine standing within the bed of the Mahanadi at Sonepur, whose goddess was the presiding deity of the region once known as Paschima Lanka. It is maintained in worship by the Kaibarta community of Sonepur and the wider Subarnapur district.

name: Kuttumuck Siva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple about 5 km north-east of Thrissur where the god is worshipped in the fierce Kiratha form, with subsidiary shrines to Ganapathy, Ayyappan and Vishnu. Its image is reputed to be more than three centuries old, though no records survive to confirm it; the ten-day Utsavam Pallivetta ending in the Aarattu is its chief festival.
story: When Tipu Sultan's Mysore army advanced on the temple, a swarm of bees is said to have risen and driven the soldiers back.

name: Lankeshwar Temple
significance: An old hilltop Shiva shrine in western Guwahati near the Gauhati University campus, held by Shaivites to be among the most sacred in the city and visited by pilgrims and tourists alike through the year.

name: Tirucherai Saranathan Temple
builtDisplay: 10th c. (Chola); later Vijayanagara and Nayak work
significance: One of the 108 Divya Desams, praised in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham and carrying inscriptions of the Chola king Parakesari Varman (906–946 CE), with later building by the Vijayanagara rulers and the Madurai Nayaks. Its granite-walled enclosure runs 380 feet on each side behind a five-tier, 120-foot gopuram, and it is the only Divya Desam where Vishnu has five consorts and the river Kaveri has a shrine of her own.
story: Vishnu is said to have appeared as a child to the river goddess Kaveri while she did penance to be reckoned the equal of the Ganges, showing her all ten of his avatars and granting her precedence during the month of Tula.

name: Laxmi Narayan Temple
significance: A small Vaishnava shrine of about 3.2 metres inside the Kapileswara temple precinct at Bhubaneswar, built with a pidha-order vimana. Its image shows Lakshmi and Narayana seated in padmasana on a lotus pedestal, with a Garuda pillar set before the entrance.

name: Labesvara Siva Temple
significance: A 15th-century sandstone Shiva temple at Bhubaneswar, locally also known as Hanumantesvara. The fabric has weathered badly, with rainwater entering the sanctum through cracks in the roof.

name: Beleswar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple on the coast of Puri district in Odisha, standing beside the sea beach that takes its name from the shrine.

name: Dakshina Mookambika Temple, North Paravur
significance: A goddess temple at North Paravur in Ernakulam district whose sanctum stands within a lotus pool, with subsidiary shrines to Ganapathy, Kartikeya, Vishnu, Hanuman and others. It is best known for Navaratri, when a music festival is held and children are initiated into letters at the Vidyarambham on Vijayadashami.
story: The ruler of Paravur, who travelled each year to the Mookambika temple at Kollur, is said to have been told by the goddess in a dream to make her image near his palace so that he could see her daily.

name: Lakhesvara Siva Temple
deity: Shiva (lingam in a circular yoni pitha)
significance: A 13th-century rekha deul on a saptaratha plan standing behind the Lingaraja market complex in Bhubaneswar, rising about 18 metres and carved with lotus and chaitya motifs. Shivaratri, Sankranti and Chandana Utsav are kept here, though seepage and wall cracks now threaten the fabric.

name: Dhari Devi Temple
deity: Dhari Devi, a form of Kali
significance: A Shakta shrine on the Alaknanda at Kalyasaur between Srinagar and Pauri Garhwal, counted among the 108 Shakta pithas and revered as the guardian deity of Uttarakhand and of the Char Dham pilgrimage. No record survives of when the first temple was raised; the image was moved on 16 June 2013 for a hydroelectric project, hours before the floods that devastated the region.
story: Dhari Devi is said to have been the youngest of seven children, killed by her brothers on an astrologer's warning and thrown into the river, her upper half coming to rest at Kalyasaur and her lower half at Kalimath.

name: Bhima Devi Temple Complex
significance: The remains of a Gurjara-Pratihara temple complex at Pinjore in Panchkula district, built between the 8th and 12th centuries on a panchayatana plan of a main shrine ringed by four subsidiary ones, comparable to work at Khajuraho and Bhubaneswar. Its sculpture spans Shaiva, Vaishnava and Shakta subjects, and the site is now an open-air museum beside the 17th-century Yadavindra Gardens.
story: The Devi Mahatmya tells of Bhimadevi manifesting in colossal form in the western Himalaya near this place to protect the sages.

name: Chittoor Sree Krishnaswamy Temple
significance: A 13th-century Krishna temple at South Chittoor near Ernakulam, founded by the Cheranelloor Swaroopam, with a square sanctum under a copper-plated pyramidal roof in the Kerala manner. It has been administered by the Cochin Devaswom Board since independence.
story: A young member of the founding family, Narayanan Kartha, is said to have dreamed that Krishna promised to travel with him inside an umbrella and to settle wherever it was set down, and the temple was raised on that spot.
